name: Araliaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project Hydrocotyle pennyworts as creeping wetland herbs with peltate orbicular leaves, axillary umbel-type inflorescences and strongly flattened ribbed fruits, while explaining the older Apiaceae/Hydrocotyloideae placement.

taxonomy_scope.project_teaching_treatment: Current Kew: Hydrocotyle in Araliaceae, order Apiales.
taxonomy_scope.historical_note: Older floras commonly treat Hydrocotyle in Apiaceae/Umbelliferae. Preserve that placement as source/search provenance, not as a second project family.

project_scope.note: Both are accepted current species and current Kew native ranges include Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the creeping stem and leaf attachment. Project Hydrocotyle roots at nodes and carries nearly round peltate leaves on long petioles.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Creeping perennial wetland herbs, rooting at nodes. Leaves simple, usually peltate in the two project species, with radiating primary veins and membranous stipules.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Tiny bisexual flowers in axillary pedunculate umbels or superposed whorls. Calyx teeth minute or obsolete; petals small.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Strongly laterally compressed, ribbed schizocarp-like fruit with two mericarps; stylopodium reduced/obsolete.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Creeping pennywort + centrally peltate round leaf + tiny umbel/whorled umbel + flattened ribbed fruit = project Araliaceae/Hydrocotyle.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: creeping node/root → peltate leaf → simple umbel vs verticillate spike → tiny flower → flattened ribbed fruit → Apiaceae-placement card
visual_lesson.intro: Pennywort looks like a tiny aquatic umbrella. The leaf gets attention first, but the arrangement of the flower clusters is what separates the two project species.

steps.title: 1 · Find the peltate attachment
steps.look_for: Petiole enters near the center of a round blade, with veins radiating outward.

steps.title: 2 · Follow the runner to a rooting node
steps.look_for: Slender horizontal stem rooting where nodes contact wet substrate.

steps.title: 3 · H. umbellata door
steps.look_for: A simple or proliferous umbrella-like umbel on a slender peduncle rather than multiple stacked flower whorls.
steps.why_it_matters: Primary project split from H. verticillata.

steps.title: 4 · H. verticillata door
steps.look_for: An interrupted spike of several small umbels/verticils stacked along the peduncle.
steps.why_it_matters: The 'verticillata' name becomes a visible memory aid.

steps.title: 5 · Flatten the fruit concept
steps.look_for: Broadly ellipsoid fruit compressed side-to-side with conspicuous ribs.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds reproductive confirmation after the tiny flowers disappear.

steps.title: 6 · Explain the family-name change
steps.look_for: Older Apiaceae/Umbelliferae references → current Kew Araliaceae for Hydrocotyle.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents older keys from looking like a project error.

comparisons.title: Hydrocotyle project species
comparisons.rule: H. umbellata centers on a simple/proliferous umbel; H. verticillata forms an interrupted vertical series of flower whorls/umbels.

comparisons.title: Araliaceae/Hydrocotyle vs Apiaceae
comparisons.rule: The project follows the current Kew placement of Hydrocotyle in Araliaceae, but older Apiaceae morphology references remain useful because family circumscription changed.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not identify the two pennywort species from leaf shape alone; their peltate leaves overlap strongly. Inflorescence architecture is much safer.

genera.fast_cue: creeping wetland herb + peltate round leaf + tiny umbel-type inflorescence + flattened ribbed fruit
